prompts.study.explain.detailed: Explain “[topic]” for [level]. I already know: [what I know]. I don't understand: [what is unclear]. Start with a simple analogy, then explain in 5–7 short paragraphs with one real-life example. Flag anything you're unsure about. Finish with 3 self-check questions and don't show the answers.
prompts.study.explain.refine: The second paragraph is still unclear to me. Explain it differently, with another example and no jargon.
prompts.study.explain.check: Here's how I understand “[topic]”: [my summary]. Point out inaccuracies and explain what to fix, but don't rewrite my text.
prompts.study.simple.short: Explain “[topic]” so someone with no background can follow.
prompts.study.simple.detailed: Explain “[topic]” in plain words: short sentences, no jargon, and if a term is unavoidable, explain it right away. Keep it under [length]. Add one everyday example. End with one sentence on what this simplification leaves out.
prompts.study.simple.refine: Make it even simpler, as if for a 10-year-old, without distorting the meaning.
prompts.study.simple.check: Ask me 3 simple questions to see whether I've understood “[topic]”. Ask one at a time and wait for my answer.
prompts.study.analogy.detailed: Give 3 different analogies for “[topic]” for [audience]: one from home life, one from sport or games, one from nature. For each, say what matches the real thing and what doesn't. Mark which analogy is most accurate.
prompts.study.analogy.refine: I liked the analogy about [analogy]. Extend it to the next step of the topic.
prompts.study.analogy.check: I came up with my own analogy for “[topic]”: [my analogy]. Where is it right and where is it misleading?
prompts.study.term.detailed: Break down the term “[term]” from [subject] for [level]: 1) a one-sentence definition; 2) the word's parts and origin; 3) an example of use; 4) which terms it's often confused with and how it differs. If it has several meanings, say which one applies to [subject].
prompts.study.term.refine: Give two more examples of “[term]” used in different situations.
prompts.study.term.check: Check my definition of “[term]”: [my definition]. What's right and what's missing?
prompts.study.compare.detailed: Compare “[concept 1]” and “[concept 2]” for [level]. Make a table: definition, key feature, example, where it's used. Below the table, say what they have in common and one typical mistake when people mix them up.
prompts.study.compare.refine: Add a “[criterion]” row to the table and an example where the difference is most visible.
prompts.study.compare.check: Give me 4 statements and I'll say which concept each belongs to. Then check my answers.
prompts.study.plan.short: Make a plan to learn “[topic]” in [time].
prompts.study.plan.detailed: Make a plan to learn “[topic]” for [level] over [time], [time per day] per day. Split it into stages from easy to hard. For each stage: what to study, how to self-check, how long it takes. Keep one day for review. Format it as a table.
prompts.study.plan.refine: I couldn't finish [stage]. Rebuild the rest of the plan so I still meet the deadline.
prompts.study.plan.check: Ask me one question per stage of the plan to see whether I'm ready to move on.
prompts.study.exam.short: Help me prepare for a [subject] exam in [time].
prompts.study.exam.detailed: I'm preparing for a [subject] exam in [time]. Topics: [topic list]. My weakest: [weak topics]. Make a day-by-day plan: weak topics first, then review the rest, then a practice test at the end. Add how to check myself each day without AI.
prompts.study.exam.refine: Make a 10-question practice test on [topics] of varying difficulty. Show answers only after mine.
prompts.study.exam.check: Here are my practice test answers: [answers]. Explain the mistakes and tell me which topics to review again.
prompts.study.cards.detailed: Make [number] flashcards on “[topic]” for [level]. Format: “Question | Answer”, answers no longer than 15 words. Mix types: definitions, examples, “why” questions. Use only this material: [material].
prompts.study.cards.refine: Cards [numbers] are too easy. Replace them with harder ones that test understanding, not memory.
prompts.study.cards.check: Quiz me on the cards one at a time in random order. Repeat the ones I get wrong more often.
prompts.study.gaps.short: Ask me questions on “[topic]” to find what I understand poorly.
prompts.study.gaps.detailed: Test my understanding of “[topic]” for [level]. Ask one question at a time, from easy to hard. After each answer say what's right, but don't explain yet. After 6 questions, list my gaps and suggest what to review first.
prompts.study.gaps.refine: Explain the gap “[gap]” briefly and give one exercise to reinforce it.
prompts.study.gaps.check: A couple of days later: ask me 3 questions again on my gaps only and tell me if I've improved.
prompts.study.steps.short: Explain step by step how to solve this problem: [problem].
prompts.study.steps.detailed: Help me understand how to solve: [problem]. Don't solve it all at once. Give the first step and a hint, wait for my attempt, then the next step. If I make a mistake, explain exactly where. At the end, name the rule or idea used here.
prompts.study.steps.refine: Show another way to solve the same problem and compare it with the first.
prompts.study.steps.check: Give me a similar problem with different numbers. I'll solve it myself and you check only my answer and method.

verify.study.explain: Check definitions and key facts against your textbook. If the analogy feels off, ask where it stops working.
verify.study.simple: Make sure nothing important was lost: compare the simple version with the textbook definition.
verify.study.analogy: Every analogy is imperfect. Ask where it differs from reality and remember that difference.
verify.study.term: Compare the definition with a subject dictionary or textbook. A term can mean different things in different fields.
verify.study.compare: Check each table row against your textbook: in comparisons AI sometimes adds properties that aren't there.
verify.study.plan: Compare the plan with your syllabus or textbook: AI may skip a required topic or add an extra one.
verify.study.exam: Compare the topic list with the official exam question list from your teacher or syllabus.
verify.study.cards: Check each card against your notes: a mistake on a card gets memorised just as well as a correct answer.
verify.study.gaps: If the AI says you “know it all”, test yourself again with textbook problems.
verify.study.steps: Redo the solution yourself without hints and check the answer by substitution or with the textbook answers.
